purpose: Teach: 煮込み/梅干/生姜/八百屋/盆栽/草木/別世界/締めくくり

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、お前の煮込み料理、毎週楽しみだった。
lines.en: When you were younger, I used to look forward to your stewed dishes every week.
lines.style: Soft nostalgia. The opening hangs gently in the air—no rush. Voice settles into the memory, warm but untethered. Long, unhurried pace. A man sitting still, letting time move backward.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。梅干、ぬか床で漬けてた、覚えてる?
lines.en: Yes. The plums I'd pickle in nukadoko—do you remember?
lines.style: Bright recognition, then gentle. A small smile in the voice. Quick at the start, then slows to linger on the shared memory. Alive with the pleasure of being understood.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 生姜湯、冬の朝の定番だな。
lines.en: Ginger tea was the winter-morning habit, wasn't it.
lines.style: Quiet agreement. Voice finds the rhythm of habit—steady, almost meditative. No question mark at the end, though the words sit softly. He's speaking to himself as much as to her.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 近所の八百屋、店主が代わったわね。
lines.en: The greengrocer nearby—the owner's changed now.
lines.style: Observational, a touch wry. Voice lifts slightly on the acknowledgment of change. Not sad, but marking time passing. She's noticing what he would have noticed. Comfortable in shared observation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 盆栽の世話、最近、楽しみで仕方ない。
lines.en: Tending the bonsai—I can't tell you how much I enjoy it lately.
lines.style: Genuine delight underneath. Warm attack. Voice opens on 'tending'—there's real pleasure here. Pace picks up slightly, almost surprised by his own contentment. Breath reaches toward her, not away.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お庭の草木、二人で育てた歴史よ。
lines.en: The garden plants we've grown together—that's our whole history.
lines.style: Reverent, grounded. Opens softly on 'garden'—she's speaking of something sacred without naming it. Slow, deliberate pace. Each word carries the weight of decades. Slight tremor of emotion held steady.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 金婚式、別世界のように感動したな。
lines.en: Our golden anniversary—it moved me like stepping into another world.
lines.style: Overwhelmed but contained. Voice reaches toward wonder, then pulls back into composure. He's remembering a specific moment of grace. Breath catches slightly. Pace slows on 'another world.' Almost reverent.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 人生の締めくくり、二人で穏やかに迎えたいわ。
lines.en: As we close this chapter, I want us to meet what comes with calm, together.
lines.style: Settled certainty. She's not asking—stating something she's decided long ago. Voice is firm and tender at once. The final sentence carries the full weight of a lifetime. Opens clearly, closes with quiet resolve. No uncertainty.
